q: Which of the following holds true for bond prices and yields?
o: They move in the same direction
Bond prices are independent of yields
e: Bond price moves inversely to yield. When yields rise, prices fall (and vice versa). Longer-maturity bonds are more sensitive.

q: Modified duration of a bond measures:
o: % change in bond price for 1% change in yield
Time to recover the bond's price from cash flows
e: Modified duration = % price change for a 1% yield move (linear approximation). Macaulay duration is the weighted-average time to receive cash flows; Modified ≈ Macaulay / (1 + YTM).
EPS = Net Profit / Weighted Average Shares Outstanding. Diluted EPS adds in potential dilution from convertibles and ESOPs.

q: Yield To Maturity (YTM) of a bond is:
o: The discount rate that equates future cash flows to current price
The face value divided by price
e: YTM is the IRR of holding the bond to maturity — the discount rate that makes the present value of future cash flows equal the current price.
